fns.desc: hostapd_ctrl_set_key (CONFIG_TESTING_OPTIONS): key_len = (os_strchr(pos,' ')-pos)/2 is derived directly from the attacker/test-harness-controlled SET_KEY ctrl_iface command string with NO upper-bound check against sizeof(key) before 'if (hexstr2bin(pos, key, key_len) < 0) return -1;' at line 2220 writes key_len bytes into the fixed-size stack buffer 'u8 key[WPA_TK_MAX_LEN]' (32 bytes, ctrl_iface.c:2185). A hex key string longer than 64 hex chars overflows the 32-byte stack buffer. hexstr2bin() (src/utils/common.c:171) performs no internal bounds checking, writing exactly len bytes. sqc's ARR39-C/ARR38-C findings in this same file flagged unrelated sizeof-double-scaling issues but missed this real unbounded-length-into-fixed-buffer write.
